extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs; Department of the Interior officials; Indian agency superintendents and agents
extracted.subtask_description: An official annual report from a United States Indian agent describing agency operations, needs, outputs, and recommending actions (buildings, equipment, staffing, education, agriculture, and health). Used to evaluate agency performance and request departmental support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate infrastructure needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists specific buildings and facilities urgently needed (new mess-house, new stable 30x60 with 10x60 sheds, warehouse for agricultural implements 30x100, elevator for storing crop, new flour-mill with increased capacity and improved machinery, building for an industrial boarding-school for both sexes to accommodate at least 50 pupils, new residence for the agent, root/vegetable house to receive and preserve seed potatoes, onions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items 'should be built this season, if possible' or 'should be built immediately' — urgency and specific sizes/dimensions are provided; justification includes protecting crops, improving processes, and accommodating pupils and staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition and improvement of Indian housing
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that Indian houses are 'entirely constructed by themselves' (except doors/windows) of logs with pole/slab roofs covered with clay; they are 'very good and comfortable houses, except when it rains', and 'with the addition of boards for floors, and shingle roofs, they will make a better appearance'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: evaluate Indian housing on construction method, weatherproofing (floors/shingles), and potential for inexpensive improvements that raise comfort and appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial and shop productivity and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics and functions of mills and shops under supervision (flour-mill grinds 300,000–400,000 lbs wheat per annum; saw-mill output 81,600 feet of lumber; tin-shop manufactured all tinware and stovepipe used by over 2,000 Indians; carpenter and blacksmith shop outputs and repairs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess shops by production volumes, range of repairs/manufacture, and staffing (noting that only a few white supervisors were employed while most workmen were Indians). Use these as measures of self-sufficiency and effectiveness of industrial training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship and local training capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation and practice of training apprentices in trades (six Indian apprentices learning trades: four carpenters, two blacksmiths; proposal to open a harness shop where two or more apprentices can be taught to make and repair harness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: existence, number, and continuation of apprenticeship positions; low marginal expense to set up training shops; expected outcome is skilled local labor and increased self-reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Farm acreage, cropping, and yields as performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed acreage and estimated yields (agency farm: 210 acres wheat, 40 oats, 80 sod-corn, 10 orchard; Indian farms total acres and yields; reclaimed acres, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use acreage under cultivation and estimated/actual yields per crop to evaluate agricultural progress and productivity; include acreage reclaimed from weeds as positive indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Farm financial performance (expense vs. crop value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculation of farm expense including seed, fence, building, and delivery ($1,570) versus value of estimated crop ($2,560.50), yielding a profit ($990.50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: evaluate farms by accounting expense, crop value, and net profit to justify expenditures and future investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nursery and orchard establishment and survival rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Planting of trees (apple varieties, cherries, plums, grapes, currants, gooseberries, raspberries) and formation of a nursery; survival/growth rates noted (e.g., 'Nearly if not quite 90 per cent of the fruit trees are growing finely; of the small fruit only about 50 per cent are now growing').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure success of fruit introduction by planting numbers and percentage survival; use as indicator of suitability of fruit-growing and Indians' care (pruning, mulching).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization of farm machinery to reduce costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that the department adopt some particular reaper and mower for certain agencies so that only one manufacture is used per agency, reducing the variety of 'extras' or repairs stock and lowering repair delays and expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: standardize equipment per agency to minimize spare-parts inventory, reduce emergency procurement costs, decrease downtime in harvest, and lower total cost of ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock-raising program and genetic improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to purchase 500–800 head of stock-cattle per year for a few years, with bulls being thoroughbreds or high grades only, so Indians can raise their own beef and relieve government expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate stock programs by numbers purchased annually, breed quality of breeding stock, and projected self-sufficiency in meat supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education provision and enrollment as a civilizing metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of boarding-school started for Indian children (first session grew from 3 to 27 pupils), need for more facilities to accommodate expected demand; 'This school is the very foundation of the civilization of these two bands of Indians.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure educational success by school capacity, enrollment numbers, trend in pupils, and facilities (dormitories, day-schools); prioritize constructing appropriate school buildings to expand access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary and medical provision (need for agency physician)
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting considerable sickness and deaths among Indians due to unchecked diseases, and urging sending a physician at salary $800–900 to improve health outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: presence of an agency physician, morbidity/mortality rates, and access to medical care; recommend budgetary trade-offs to provide medical personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewarding improvement with implements and settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy of issuing implements/assistance at annuity time to those who had 'made the greatest improvement' to enable them to continue without interference; method used to locate twenty new families successfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: target aid to those who have demonstrated improvement or industriousness to incentivize settlement and self-reliance; use distribution policy as a management tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fencing and land protection standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of substantial barbed-wire fence with cedar posts 16 feet apart to enclose farm tracts and reclaimed land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate enclosure adequacy by fence type and spacing to protect cultivated land and support irrigation/production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclamation and expansion of cultivated acreage
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of reclaimed acres (e.g., reclaimed 40 acres formerly broken but grown to weeds; broken additional acres in 1879) and increases in acreage under cultivation year-over-year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: area newly broken or reclaimed and total acreage under cultivation as indicators of agricultural expansion and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition and repair of agency buildings and mills
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent note that buildings, mills, fences, etc., were dilapidated on assumption of charge; recommendation for repairs, rebuilding, or overhauling mills (e.g., addition of smutter for cleaning wheat, engine/boiler work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess agencies by state of physical plant and prioritize repairs or rebuilding; tie repair requests to operational needs (mill capacity, storage, seed protection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Indian labor and labor-management practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations on Indian labor: many useful works done by Indians (cutting logs, building, brick-making, freighting) and that young men may tire early but increase stamina with repetition; also notes on oversubscription for hired work (more wagons offered than needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: organization and supervision of Indian labor, training progression, selection/allocation methods for work opportunities, and controls to avoid claims for unauthorized labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Indian property and redress for military seizures
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint about military collecting and selling cattle/stock belonging to friendly Indians (55 head sold at $5 each) and suggestion that 'some relief should be afforded the Indian owners' and reporting for departmental instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: protection and restitution mechanisms for Indian-owned property seized by others (including military), and tracking of such incidents in reports to secure departmental action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation boundary marking and survey accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint that indistinct reservation line prevents definite action against white settlers squatting; suggestion that the line 'be rerun and permanently marked'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess need for clear surveying and permanent markers of reservation boundaries to prevent encroachment and future disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics of social progress (dress, church membership, volunteer activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of indicators such as number wearing citizens' dress, church membership increases, voluntary subscriptions (e.g., $125 toward a bell, $100 toward salary of native preacher), and missionary activity to measure progress toward 'civilization.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: quantify social/cultural indicators (dress adoption rates, church membership, voluntary contributions) as part of evaluation of assimilation and community development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic utilization of natural resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of sale of timber/wood (600 cords and 30,000 feet of logs) yielding $4,800 and construction of houses with lumber bought by Indians at 'trifling expense to the government'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate income generation from resource sales and whether revenue or local purchases reduce government expense and facilitate independent housing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural extension measures (irrigation, ditches, gardens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of constructing an irrigating ditch over a mile long, garden cultivation at the Kamia school, and irrigation potential along river lands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: presence and maintenance of irrigation infrastructure and demonstration gardens as indicators of agricultural advancement and food security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative population and demographic accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed enumeration of tribe populations (men, women, boys, girls, totals) used to show slight increases and to feed planning for supplies and programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use demographic tables and counts to plan annuities, supplies, schooling and to monitor population trends.
